title: sdk(py): improve default retry/backoff + error messages for 429/timeouts
author: Monica Patel
description:
Context: We’ve had repeat Support escalations where customers hit frequent 429s or timeouts and the Python SDK’s guidance/defaults weren’t helping them converge quickly on a safe retry strategy. This PR updates the SDK defaults and error surfaces to make the “do the right thing” path clearer, and links customers to the canonical troubleshooting pages.

What changed:
- Default retry policy: implement exponential backoff w/ jitter for retryable errors and respect Retry-After when present.
  - Retries apply to: HTTP 429, 408, 409 (transient), 5xx, and network-level timeouts/connection resets.
  - Retries do NOT apply to: 4xx other than 408/409/429.
  - Hard cap on total elapsed retry time to avoid runaway waits (defaults: max_retries=6, max_retry_wait=20s, max_elapsed=60s).
- Better error messages:
  - 429 RateLimitError now includes: request_id (when available), whether Retry-After was provided, and a short “next steps” block (backoff + verify project quota / consider Dedicated).
  - Timeout errors include: configured timeout, recommendation to increase read timeout for long generations, and streaming guidance.
- Docs + examples:
  - README snippet for configuring retries/timeouts.
  - Added a small cookbook example that demonstrates safe backoff and logs request IDs.
  - Links to known-issues pages:
    - https://docs.redwoodinference.com/known-issues/429-throttling-and-quota
    - https://docs.redwoodinference.com/known-issues/streaming-disconnects

Why:
- SUP-4922 (self-serve): customer launched, saw frequent 429s; existing SDK example used naive fixed sleep and no jitter; resolution required manual guidance.
- SUP-4921 (enterprise/dedicated): intermittent timeouts/disconnects; error messages didn’t surface request_id consistently, slowing triage.

Notes/compat:
- No API breaking changes. We are changing defaults (retries enabled + tuned) but config remains fully overridable via ClientOptions.
- Streaming: we do not automatically retry mid-stream responses; error text explicitly calls out recommended client reconnect behavior.

Testing:
- Added unit tests around Retry-After parsing, jitter bounds, and non-retryable 4xx behavior.
- Ran examples against staging with induced 429 + timeout via gateway test harness.

Follow-ups:
- We should align TS + Go SDK behavior with the same retry classification (tracked in ENG-2841).
commits: sdk(py): add RetryPolicy w/ exp backoff + jitter + Retry-After support
sdk(py): improve RateLimitError and TimeoutError messaging (include request_id + next steps)
docs/examples: update README + add cookbook for 429/timeouts troubleshooting
tests: cover retry classification and backoff limits
changed_files: redwood_sdk/client.py (wire retry policy + surface request_id in exceptions)
redwood_sdk/_http.py (respect Retry-After, cap elapsed time, better timeout mapping)
review_conversation: Ibrahim Khan (review): The default retry set looks good, but can we confirm we’re not retrying non-idempotent requests in a way that surprises customers? Specifically, generation POSTs can have side effects for billing/usage. Suggest we (a) only retry on connection-level failures where the request likely didn’t reach us, and (b) ensure we log/return request_id for any server response so Support can de-dupe. Also: please ensure we obey Retry-After exactly (seconds + HTTP date).

Monica Patel (author): Agree. I updated classification to: retry 429/5xx/408/409 only when we have a server response (so request_id captured); for connection errors/timeouts we retry but we cap elapsed time and include a note in docs that retries may result in multiple attempts. Retry-After parsing now supports integer seconds and HTTP-date; tests added.

Owen Phillips (review): Can we add an explicit snippet in the error message telling customers what to send Support? (request_id, region, model, timestamp). SUP-4922 took too long because we didn’t have request IDs from the first email.

Monica Patel (author): Added a short “Include in support ticket:” block for RateLimitError + TimeoutError when request_id is present; also updated cookbook example to log request_id + x-redwood-region if available.

Alex Martinez (review): Please link to the canonical known-issues pages (Docs is publishing refreshed pages) and keep wording consistent with Support. The README text currently says “increase quota” without clarifying project vs org limits.

Monica Patel (author): Updated links to match the new slugs and aligned the README wording to “verify org/project quotas and per-route rate limits”; also pointed to the 429 known-issues page as the source of truth.
Priya Shah (review): +1. One nit: in 429 message, avoid promising timelines (“usually clears in X minutes”). Keep it as safe steps only.
Monica Patel (author): Removed the timeline language and kept it action-oriented. Thanks.
Ibrahim Khan (final review): Looks good now. Approving.
release_notes: - Python SDK now uses a safer default retry/backoff policy for transient failures (429/5xx/timeouts) and respects Retry-After when provided. - Improved 429/timeout error messages with request_id and clearer troubleshooting steps; added README + example guidance.
